purpose.summary: Run the existing upstream Chronik indexer and read router in an explicitly compiled and opted-in bounded regtest bitcoind, with native-owned startup and joined stop.
scope: Add a default-OFF regtest service build and runtime capability, restricted to unpruned regtest with plugins and Qt OFF.
Wait for native import and actual mempool restoration before opening the existing upstream indexer; retain its writers, token parsing and read handlers.
Own the callback worker and atomic ephemeral loopback HTTP listener until joined shutdown before scheduler/native resource teardown.
Exercise real daemon mining, nonempty parent/child mempool reopen, confirmation, disconnect/reconsider, raw transaction parity and index-only failed-root refusal.
Preserve bounded source limits, ordinary dormant/compiled-out controls, immutable donor/dependency inputs, historical records and explicit proof ceilings.
exclusions: No mainnet or testnet activation, consensus or native mempool policy change, external listener, websocket, broadcast or operator plugin.
No server access, deployment, cutover, release, desktop integration, automatic rebuild/wipe or production crash-recovery claim.
No incoming report, binary, datadir, host metadata, private history, operator configuration or credentials.

commands: Build the independent compiled-out profile with all upstream/plugin/observer flags OFF; execute the existing native zero-subsidy mining and positive-stop smoke.
expected_results: Native mining and shutdown work without linking Rust/Chronik; no Chronik state or external peer connection is created.

commands: Build separate archival and plugin profiles with BUILD_CHRONIK_UPSTREAM_REGTEST=OFF; run unchanged exact native selections and dormant daemon controls. Keep the enabled daemon build independent.
expected_results: No Python plugin implementation is selected; setup refuses before plugin files or state are created. Linking upstream alone starts no daemon index or listener.

commands: Build BUILD_CHRONIK_UPSTREAM_REGTEST=ON, upstream link/archival ON, plugins/observer/Qt OFF. Run regtest_service_self_test.py and regtest_service.py with three complete repetitions, plus retained native component selections.
expected_results: Actual daemon lifecycle, nonempty native mempool restart, confirmation/disconnect/reconsider and byte parity pass; joined stops close listeners and leases; a failed index does not stop native mining. No production or independent reproduction claim.

scenarios.command: Run the new regtest_service.py witness in a separately built real bitcoind: default OFF, wrong-network/pruned refusals, enabled genesis startup, mining, nonempty parent/child pool restart, confirmation/disconnect/reconsider, byte parity, failed-root refusal and joined stops. Retain the original native matrices and plugin restart witnesses in their separate profiles.
expected_results: Three real-daemon lifecycle repetitions with identical result predicates; 15 fresh daemon processes including dormant and exact scope-refusal controls, with verified cleanup before report creation.
Native accepted transaction bytes and exact indexed pool membership agree after restart, confirmation and reorg; failed-root refusal leaves native mining functional.
Separate fixture profiles retain enabled 48 cases/2385 assertions and disabled 45 cases/2291 assertions per repetition. These remain component observations, not this daemon's production readiness.
failure_conditions: Wrong exact case/assertion selection, stale or changed source/view, mismatched plugin accepted, identity rewritten, disabled guard bypass, failed root adopted, native authority effect, skip, timeout, nonzero exit, instability or incomplete cleanup.

scenarios.command: Execute real-daemon pending and confirmed reopen witnesses from regtest_service.py. Keep the inherited 288-block observer restart scenario separate: the new daemon uses 103 zero-subsidy blocks and makes no full-window crash-recovery claim.
expected_results: Pending native parent/child pool survives actual process restart; confirmed raw bytes remain identical after a later healthy reopen.
The small bounded daemon witness does not establish production crash recovery or a complete 288-block startup stress result.
failure_conditions: Restart drift, stale query, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Existing observer profile only, retained by chronik-port-core.yml: Run the HTTP and observer full-reindex canaries.
expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.
Canonical confirmed bytes are unchanged after full reindex and query admission remains opt-in.
failure_conditions: Stale index, response drift, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Existing observer profile only, retained by chronik-port-core.yml: Run the HTTP and observer chainstate-reindex canaries.
expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.
Ordered accepted callbacks rebuild the same confirmed protobuf without changing validation.
failure_conditions: Stale index, response drift, validation effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Existing observer profile only, retained by chronik-port-core.yml: Run the two-role pruning canary with fresh-pruned bootstrap and concurrent requests during already-indexed pruning.
expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.

Concurrent old-transaction reads are either canonical 200 or protobuf 503, never a fabricated or partial response. After file removal the old transaction is 503; a retained recent transaction remains 200 and the node continues at its accepted height.
The pre-existing fresh-pruned observer bootstrap failure remains isolated from node correctness.
failure_conditions: Silent 404 for an indexed pruned transaction, fabricated fallback, partial result, node shutdown, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Existing observer profile only, retained by chronik-port-core.yml: Run feature_chronik_token_http.py: extend to height 290 in bounded batches, disconnect below the retained projection anchor, reconsider, verify mismatched restart leaves HTTP disabled, then explicitly full-reindex. Separately exercise upstream retained-anchor and source-generation contradictions; the fixture observer closes while native progress continues.
expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.
Both known and unknown token/transaction IDs return protobuf 503 after observer closure, never stale 200 or misleading 404.

Node RPC and chain selection continue; reconsider does not reopen observation. A persistent-tip mismatch disables HTTP on restart and logs recovery=reindex. Explicit full reindex restores canonical token metadata and byte-identical confirmed transaction output.
failure_conditions: Any accepted response after irreversible closure, missing-ID 404 from a degraded view, HTTP serving from a mismatched restarted runtime, missing mismatch diagnostic, failed canonical reindex recovery, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

limitations: Experimental startup is synchronous before peers start. Stalled storage can delay initialization or joined shutdown; there is no hard I/O latency or unrestricted service-availability guarantee.

Experimental bounded unpruned regtest only: height <= 2000, native index/pool limits <= 4096, retained capture window 288 blocks, callback budget 128 and serialized payload budget 64 MiB. These are not measured RSS/heap or full-chain performance bounds.
Open Question / record-review-only with no incoming evidence. Local/CI executions do not automatically establish independent reproduction or production readiness.
Plugins are OFF in the daemon service profile. Separate existing synthetic plugin tests are not operator plugin compatibility or Python sandboxing evidence.
Mainnet, public exposure, crash recovery, production DB migration, Linux server shadow validation, deployment/cutover and desktop integration remain outside this lot.
Dependencies in Cargo.lock are unchanged and registry inputs locked; system dependencies/SDK/runner images remain unlocked. Existing upstream security alerts remain open.
counterevidence: A complete local ten-repetition retained matrix passed its bridge, owned-startup and capture/query groups, then refused during the stop/reopen group and created no passing report. Its exact refusal class was not retained by that invocation. Three later isolated stop/reopen suites passed 13 cases/307 assertions each under the same 60-second deadline. A later full invocation passed all 45 cases/2291 assertions per repetition across 70 fresh processes, without concurrent builds and without changing any selection, deadline, signature comparison or cleanup criterion. These later passes do not establish the earlier cause or erase the refusal.

The first retained-matrix CLI invocation rejected the newly named regtest repetition profile before launching a native test. The profile was added explicitly with the same 45-case/2291-assertion plugin-disabled selection, and the synthetic profile-selection test now covers it. No case, assertion, deadline or cleanup criterion was relaxed.

The first real-daemon attempt exited before Chronik initialization because the runner supplied invalid native minrelaytxfee=0 and dustrelayfee=0 arguments. The runner incorrectly classified that exit as a warmup deadline. Diagnosis identified the native argument refusal; those arguments were removed, existing native synthetic fee priorities are explicit, and an exited-process rejection self-test was added. No startup deadline or native relay policy was relaxed.
The preceding public PR54 tested a fixture-owned upstream worker and router, not a daemon service. This lot must obtain real-process observations rather than relabel those component tests.
A native shutdown flag can race an in-flight capture. Cancellation must not create a persistent corruption marker, and Stop must run while the native callback scheduler is still alive.
An ephemeral port reserved and then dropped can be taken before rebinding. The actual upstream listener now binds port zero atomically and reports its own bound address.
Prior timeout/refusal observations in ERGON-CHANGE-0048 remain preserved there. Subsequent passes do not establish their cause.

Small zero-value regtest transactions establish mechanics only, not economically funded ALP circulation, arbitrary plugins, mainnet history or production readiness. Existing native prioritisetransaction adds a synthetic selection priority of 1000000 fixoshis per transaction; no fee or coin value is actually created or paid.
